key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants work as coupled biomechanical-biomaterial systems, where geometry, graded coatings, and gait-phase loading must be optimized together to achieve durable bone-implant integration.
engineering_relevance: The paper highlights that translating these implants to clinic depends on validated finite-element workflows, fatigue/coating durability testing, and patient-realistic mechanical loading conditions.
method: Systematic review of distal weight-bearing implant design, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of finite element analysis, functionally graded materials, graded Ti-HAp architectures, and in-vivo evidence
evidence_signal: The evidence base is still early-stage, with more than half of the empirical studies remaining at the bench or simulation level and relatively few animal or human/clinical validations.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM concepts are promising, but much of the support comes from analog biomaterial studies rather than DWBI-specific clinical validation.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
